references.text: God commands Noah to take pairs of all living creatures with him to preserve them through the flood
The clean and unclean animals enter the ark just as God had commanded Noah
Noah offers sacrifices from the clean animals after the flood – this explains why seven pairs of the clean animals were needed
The Mosaic Law gives detailed regulations concerning clean and unclean animals
Regulations about clean and unclean animals in Deuteronomy
Peter's vision regarding clean and unclean animals – God abolishes the distinction in the new covenant
Direct narrative context where 7:2 specifies the exception (seven pairs of clean animals) to the general rule in 6:19 (two of each kind).
Direct narrative context where verse 4 is the introductory part of the same instruction that is completed in verse 2.
